knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. What does Empirical Bayes typically estimate from collateral/portfolio data that a fully specified Bayesian approach would take as prior input?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: EB estimates prior/hyperparameters (e.g. mean/variance of the risk parameter distribution) from data, then forms credibility premiums.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Refuse: 'Empirical Bayes is just another name for Bayesian.' What differs?
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse identity. EB estimates prior pieces from data; full Bayes treats prior as given belief — assumptions differ.
